newsitem.title: USA: Brent mixed in late US trade, Gulf Coast crowded.
newsitem.headline: Brent mixed in late US trade, Gulf Coast crowded.

text.p: Benchmark North Sea was mixed in late U.S. trading Tuesday while intermonth spreads were steady, traders said.
Three partial paper Brent cargoes for March changed hands at $22.00/22.43/22.45 a barrel, compared to the IPE settlement price of $22.35 a barrel.
Feb/March Brent traded at 34 cents, while March/April was dealt at 43 cents, steady with late-day ranges, traders said.
Meanwhile, foreign crudes from Latin America and across the Atlantic continue to crowd into the U.S. Gulf Coast even though margins there are weak amid a series of refinery turnarounds.
Transatlantic trade continues to flourish, reflecting the open arbitrage between West Texas Intermediate and Brent. The March spread stood around $1.80-90 a barrel late in the day.
A major crude trader sold a ULCC of Brent into the Gulf, arriving February 9-13, at March WTI minus 25 cents a barrel.
"(The trader) made a killing because he sold on the basis of only four cargoes," said a broker of the transaction. A ULCC carries six cargoes.

At least half of a VLCC of Brent arriving February 20-25 was also sold at between March WTI minus five to 35 cents, traders said. They added that the company that is selling is likely to keep one million barrels for its own system.
On the Latin American front, Argentina's YPF is selling 950,000 barrels of Canadon Seco crude for loading February 24-25, trade sources said.

The formerly state-controlled oil company is asking a discount of $1.95 a barrel to benchmark West Texas Intermediate for loading onto a large vessel, or a $2.35 a barrel discount for loading onto smaller vessels, they said.
The loading terminal is Caleta Olivia on the south Atlantic coast.
Previous buyers include Brazil's state-owned Petrobras, U.S. Gulf Coast refiners and traders.
Elsewhere, Chile's state-owned oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) is seeking 960,000 barrels of crude for delivery March 10, trade sources said.
Bids will be received January 23, the sources said.
